option_relations.rationale: Ascending aortic aneurysm with thrombus formation complicating coronary perfusion describes a condition that could lead to thrombotic occlusion of the left coronary artery.
Bicuspid aortic valve with ascending aortic aneurysm and valvular thrombosis describes a condition that could lead to thrombotic occlusion of the left coronary artery.
Organized thrombus formation on native bicuspid aortic valve with ascending aortic aneurysm describes a condition that could lead to thrombotic occlusion of the left coronary artery.
Bicuspid aortic valve with thrombus-induced coronary ostial obstruction directly describes the thrombotic occlusion of the left coronary artery, as the ostial obstruction would cause the occlusion.
